main_text.head: PARAPHRASIS PSALMI DAVIDIS XXXVII, conscripta ab Adriano Borckio Pom.
main_text.p: Nete [?] malorum prosperæ res sobria De mente quatiant, neu bonis Horum caducis quicquam iniquus invide, Ventus levis quæ dissipat. Nam lacteus ceu floris aprici decor, Abit repente marcidus, Falce amputatus: nulla pars sic gaudii Sincera fluxi permanet. Tu sedulus sphæra in Deum, nec regula Vitæ, eius unquam ab orbita Deflectat: in terra mane, aruaq; fidei Fœcunda iugiter cole. Omnis voluptas in Deo sit, & tuis Votis benignus annuet. Quæcunq; versat animus illi credito, Et ipse faciet omnia. Operta virtus forte si fuit tua, Horum malignis artibus, Hanc mox apertam faciet, ut Solis quidem Certet corusco lumini. Deo quiesce, neu dolore ringere, Si prosperis successibus

page.notes: The drop-cap initial N is followed by "E te", so the first word is doubtful; marked [?]. The poem is set as continuous verse with no visible stanza breaks, so it is given as one paragraph. The catchword "Fortu-" is printed at the lower right, after the last line. Printed spellings such as "aruaq;", "Fœcunda" and "quæcunq;" are kept as they stand; u/v have been normalised (leuis to levis, uirtus to virtus, uoluptas to voluptas, uersat to versat).
